nodes.name: Saguaro
nodes.desc: A giant columnar cactus found in the wild only in the Sonoran Desert. Its nectar and fruit feed bats, doves and woodpeckers, and its trunk holds nest holes.

nodes.name: Palo verde
nodes.desc: A green-barked desert tree that acts as a nurse plant, sheltering young saguaros from frost and summer heat.

nodes.name: Velvet mesquite
nodes.desc: A deep-rooted desert legume. Its bean pods and shade are used by many animals, and tortoises draw moisture from it in dry seasons.

nodes.name: Prickly pear
nodes.desc: A pad-forming cactus whose pads and fruit are food and water for many desert animals.

nodes.name: Desert annuals & grasses
nodes.desc: Wildflowers and grasses that sprout after winter and monsoon rains and set seed quickly.

nodes.name: Kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: Seeds make up most of its diet, and snakes are its main known predators. It fends off snakes by drumming, kicking sand and kicking away strikes.

nodes.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit
nodes.desc: A big-eared hare that grazes desert plants and is a main prey of Harris's hawks and coyotes.

nodes.name: Sonoran desert tortoise
nodes.desc: A herbivore that eats mostly grasses and wildflowers, plus cactus fruit and growth. Eggs and young are taken by ravens, badgers and coyotes.

nodes.name: Collared peccary
nodes.desc: A pig-like herd animal of the desert that eats cactus pads, fruit and mesquite pods, along with roots and other plants.

nodes.name: White-winged dove
nodes.desc: Depends heavily on saguaro fruit, which can make up most of its diet in early summer.

nodes.name: Lesser long-nosed bat
nodes.desc: A migratory nectar-feeding bat and the main night pollinator of saguaro and agave flowers.

nodes.name: Desert ants
nodes.desc: Ants eat saguaro fruit, so few saguaro seeds survive to sprout, and they also gather seeds from annual plants.

nodes.name: Gambel's quail
nodes.desc: A ground bird that eats seeds, leaves and mesquite beans and is prey for hawks and snakes.

nodes.name: Gila woodpecker
nodes.desc: Eats mainly insects but also fruit and nectar. Carves nest holes in saguaros that elf owls and other birds later reuse.

nodes.name: Western diamondback rattlesnake
nodes.desc: A major snake predator of desert rodents, rabbits and ground birds.

nodes.name: Harris's hawk
nodes.desc: Hunts in family groups, which lets it take jackrabbits, plus ground squirrels, kangaroo rats and quail.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: An adaptable top predator that eats rabbits, rodents, birds and occasionally tortoises.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Intense year-round sun powers desert plants, which store water to survive the heat.

nodes.name: Winter & monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Two rainy seasons, winter rain and the summer monsoon, give this desert unusually rich plant life.

nodes.name: Desert soil
nodes.desc: Thin, mineral-rich soil that gains nutrients from plants such as palo verde, which helps shelter young saguaros.

nodes.name: Fungi, bacteria & termites
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and droppings and return nutrients to the desert soil.
